title: Grade 5 Social Studies — Daily Life and Choices in Colonial America
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on trade, labor, geography, sources, regional differences.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What made some North American colonies useful to European trading nations?
choices: They produced nothing to sell.
They were all already independent countries.
They never used ocean trade.
They supplied goods and bought imported products.

questions.question: Which crop became important to the economy of colonial Virginia?
choices: tea leaves
coffee
tobacco
bananas

questions.question: What made many colonial port towns good places for trade?
choices: The towns were far from every river and ocean.
Ships could load and unload goods there.
Trade goods could only move on mountain paths.
Roads kept all goods away from the harbor.

questions.question: Which job makes a person an apprentice?
choices: sailing past the town
learning printing while working with a skilled printer
reading a sign in a market
buying a newspaper at a shop

questions.question: Which group often did forced labor on colonial plantations?
choices: enslaved Africans and their descendants
all hired apprentices
elected assembly members as a group
all visiting traders

questions.question: Why did families who moved to the English colonies have different experiences?
choices: They all chose to move freely.
Their reasons, resources, and legal freedom differed.
They all settled in the same port at once.
They all received the same jobs and land.

questions.question: What was a reason some English settlers chose parts of New England?
choices: They were seeking the Pacific Ocean.
They planned to become independent in 1607.
They wanted to form communities around their religious beliefs.
They expected a tropical climate.

questions.question: How could location affect what a colony traded?
choices: Rivers made it impossible to travel.
Every colony sold the same crops.
Location changed the language of all people there immediately.
A harbor helped a colony send goods overseas.

questions.question: Which record best helps compare prices in two port towns?
choices: dated shop account books from both towns
an undated map showing coastlines only
one town seal
a single recipe for stew

questions.question: What can a colony's tax record help a researcher learn?
choices: what settlers dreamed about
which listed items or people were taxed
how each person felt about the tax
the exact words people spoke at dinner

questions.question: Which is an example of self-government under British rule?
choices: some eligible colonists electing members of an assembly
the colonies forming the modern U.S. Supreme Court
every colonist voting in British Parliament
every royal decision being made by children

questions.question: Why do historians distinguish indentured labor from slavery?
choices: Both guaranteed equal pay and rights.
Neither was used in English colonies.
Both always allowed workers to leave freely.
Indentured service was for a term; slavery treated people as property.

questions.question: What links ships, merchants, and farms in colonial trade?
choices: Merchants made all products aboard ships.
Farmers grew only enough to throw away.
Farm goods could be sold by merchants and carried by ship.
Ships never moved goods between places.

questions.question: Why might the same colony include more than one spoken language?
choices: Ships could carry only English speakers.
Its laws required every person to speak only one language.
There were no Indigenous languages.
Residents came from different communities and places.

questions.question: Which comparison shows different colonial economies?
choices: Every coastal and inland community had the same jobs.
Ships could reach every inland farm directly.
Port towns relied on trade; some inland communities relied more on farming.
Only inland communities used crops.

questions.question: What is a way to learn about a typical day for enslaved people?
choices: compare accounts of formerly enslaved people and records about their lives
assume every family worked under the same conditions
read only a plantation owner's price list
use only a map of modern sports stadiums

questions.question: Which would be a secondary source on a colonial settlement?
choices: a land deed from that time
a letter mailed from the settlement
a diary kept by a settler
a modern historian's explanation based on old records

questions.question: Why could relations between Native nations and colonists change over time?
choices: No one moved or traded after first contact.
Trading, land pressure, and alliances could change their choices.
Everyone spoke the same language from the start.
All communities always agreed on who owned the land.

questions.question: Which type of location often encouraged shipbuilding in New England?
choices: an inland valley cut off from waterways
a treeless desert with no trade
a coast with harbors and access to timber
a mountaintop far from any rivers

questions.question: What is one question a colonial map by itself usually cannot answer?
choices: How did different people feel about a new law?
Which feature is represented by the river symbol?
What direction was the harbor from town?
Where is the marked road?
